Start here when setup goes wrong. Most problems are one of the cases below.
If yours isn't, see [Getting help](#getting-help) at the bottom.

**Your best diagnostic tool:** from your repo folder, run

```
uv run python check_setup.py
```

Every line should start with `[OK]`. Each `[!!]` line says what to fix. Paste
the whole output into any help request.

## Codespaces

### My repo is greyed out, or I don't see "Create codespace"

Check that you accepted your repo invitation (step 2 of the [Setup guide](setup.qmd)),
and that you're on **your repo's** page: `https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>`.
Use the green **Code** button there, then the **Codespaces** tab. If the repo is
still greyed out, post on Discussions; it's a course setting the instructor can fix.

### How do I get back to my codespace?

Your repo's page > **Code** > **Codespaces** tab > click the codespace listed
there (it has a random two-word name). You can also see all of yours at
[github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces). Reuse that one codespace
all semester rather than creating new ones.

### A notebook says "No module named numpy" (or asks me to select a kernel) {#missing-package}

Python reports a missing package as `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ...`.

1. **Check the kernel.** Click **Select Kernel** (or the kernel name) at the top
   right of the notebook, choose **Python Environments**, and pick the one in
   `.venv`. Then run the cells again. This fixes it almost every time.
2. **Still missing? Run `uv sync`.** Open a terminal, a window for typing
   commands to the computer: click the **☰** menu at the top left, then
   **Terminal > New Terminal**. It opens in your repo folder, which is where
   `uv sync` has to run. Type `uv sync` and press Enter. It installs the course
   packages into your repo's `.venv` folder.
3. **Restart.** Back in the notebook, click **Restart**, then run the cells again.

Working on your own computer? See the [Positron version](#missing-package-local).

### I pressed Ctrl+W (or another shortcut) and my browser tab closed

Some shortcuts belong to the browser, not the editor. Reopen your codespace (see
above); your files are still there, and the editor saves changes automatically.

### Will I run out of codespace time?

Unlikely if you stop your codespace when you're done. Your account includes about
60 hours a month, or 90 with GitHub student benefits. Check your usage under
**Settings > Billing** on GitHub. To use less: close the tab when you're done (it
stops after 30 idle minutes), or stop it right away at
[github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) (**⋯ > Stop codespace**).
If you're about to run out, [set up your own computer](setup-local.qmd) as a backup.

### My codespace disappeared

A codespace you don't open for several weeks is deleted, along with anything not
pushed to GitHub. Create a new one from your repo page; everything you pushed is
still there. This is why every work session ends with commit and push.

### "Pull" fails after I worked in a codespace and on my laptop

Your two copies changed in different ways. Always pull when you sit down and push
when you get up. If a pull still fails, don't force anything; post the message on
Discussions.

## Your own computer: installing

### "uv is not recognized" (or "command not found")

uv is installed, but your terminal started before it was. Close every terminal
**and Positron**, reopen, and try again. If it still fails, rerun the uv install
command from the setup guide.

### I see two Pythons, or Python 3.14, or a Python I don't recognize

That's normal. Many computers already have one or more Pythons. The course uses
its own Python 3.13, which `uv sync` downloads into your repo's `.venv` folder.
You don't need to uninstall anything; you only need to **select** the `.venv` one
(see below).

## Your own computer: the Python environment

### Positron shows a red ✕ and "A dedicated Python environment is available" (or offers to "Create Python environment")

Don't click the create button. It builds a different environment from the course
one. Instead:

1. Open your repo folder (**File > Open Folder**). It's the folder that contains `pyproject.toml`.
2. Open a terminal (**Terminal > New Terminal**) and run `uv sync`.
3. Click the interpreter name at the top right of Positron and choose the Python from `.venv`.

### A command gives "No module named uv" (or a Python SyntaxError)

You typed it into the **Console**, the panel with the `>>>` prompt, which runs
Python code only. Commands such as `uv`, `git`, and `cd` go in the **Terminal**
(**Terminal > New Terminal**), whose prompt shows your folder, like
`PS C:\Users\<you>\EconS431\ps-<your-username>>`.

### `uv sync` says it can't find `pyproject.toml`

The terminal is in the wrong folder. Open your repo folder in Positron
(**File > Open Folder**), then open a new terminal; it starts in the right place.

### `uv sync` fails with "Failed to hardlink files" or "os error 396"

A sync or backup tool (OneDrive, Dropbox, and others) is blocking the file links
uv uses to save disk space. Tell uv to copy instead:

```
uv sync --link-mode=copy
```

Current course repos already include this setting, so it should only affect
older copies.

### A notebook says "No module named numpy" (or pandas, scipy, ...) {#missing-package-local}

The notebook is probably running a different Python from the course one. Click
the kernel name at the **top right of the notebook** and choose the Python from
`.venv` (it's labeled **econs431**). Then **Restart** the kernel and run the cells
again. Positron usually remembers this choice for the folder.

If the package is still missing, open a terminal (**Terminal > New Terminal**)
with your course repo folder open in Positron, run `uv sync`, then restart the
kernel again.

### `check_setup.py` says "Repo is outside a cloud-synced folder" is a problem

Your repo is inside OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud, or Google Drive. Syncing the
`.venv` folder (about 850 MB and 25,000 files) causes slowdowns and locked-file
errors. Move the repo to a folder in your home folder that doesn't sync, such as
`C:\Users\<you>\EconS431` (Windows) or `/Users/<you>/EconS431` (Mac).

Watch out: on many laptops, **Desktop and Documents are synced** (OneDrive on
Windows, iCloud on Mac) even if you never set that up. If the path contains
`OneDrive`, `Dropbox`, `iCloud`, or `Mobile Documents`, it syncs.

### My `.venv` folder is huge, and Windows won't let me delete or move it

Its size is normal: it holds compiled scientific libraries. It's never uploaded
to GitHub, and `uv sync` rebuilds it in a minute, so deleting it is always safe.

Windows refuses because a program still has its files open:

1. Quit Positron completely, including from the system tray.
2. In Task Manager, end any leftover `python.exe` processes.
3. If the folder is in OneDrive or Dropbox, pause syncing.
4. Delete it. If Windows still refuses, restart the computer and delete it before opening anything else.

## Your own computer: GitHub and Git

### The browser asks me to "Authorize Visual-Studio-Code"

That's expected. Positron is built on VS Code and uses VS Code's GitHub sign-in.
Check that the address starts with `https://github.com/`, then authorize.

### GitHub says I'm connected, but Positron says "failed to sign in to GitHub"

The browser couldn't hand the sign-in back to Positron. You don't need that
sign-in; let Git sign in on its own:

1. In Positron, open **Settings** (Ctrl+, or Cmd+,), search for `github.gitAuthentication`, uncheck it, and restart Positron.
2. When you clone, choose **Git: Clone** and **paste your repo's URL** rather than choosing "Clone from GitHub".
3. The first clone or push opens a sign-in window. Choose the browser option.

### How do I know Git can sign in to GitHub?

**Windows:** run

```
git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper
```

You should see `manager` (from `C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig`). If you see
nothing, run `git config --global credential.helper manager`.

**Mac:** install the GitHub CLI from [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com),
then run these two commands and choose the web-browser login when asked:

```
gh auth login
gh auth setup-git
```

### `check_setup.py` says "Repo is connected to GitHub" is a problem

You're working in a copy of the files rather than a clone of your GitHub repo.
Clone your repo (**Git: Clone**, paste
`https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>.git`), then run `uv sync` in
the new folder. Copy any work you want to keep into the clone.

### I get "Repository not found" (or 404) for my repo

You haven't accepted the invitation yet. Open the email from GitHub, or go to
`https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>/invitations` while signed in.

### `check_setup.py` says `git user.name` or `git user.email` isn't set

Run these once, with your own name and the email on your GitHub account:

```
git config --global user.name "First Last"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
```

### "Commit operation was cancelled due to empty commit message"

(This happens in Codespaces too.) Every commit needs a short message saying what it contains. Type one in the box
above **Commit** in Source Control (for example, "PS02 Q1-Q3 done"), then click
**Commit**. If Positron opens a `COMMIT_EDITMSG` tab instead, type the message on
its first line, then save and close the tab.

## Notebooks

### How do I tick the boxes in the PS01 checklist?

Double-click the checklist cell to edit it, change `[ ]` to `[x]`, then press
**Shift+Enter**.

### The kernel is named "econs431" (or ".venv"). Is that right?

Yes. Positron labels the course environment **econs431**; Codespaces shows it as
the Python in `.venv`. Either way it's the course environment in your repo's
`.venv` folder.

## Still stuck after 30 minutes? {#still-stuck}

If you're setting up your own computer, switch to Codespaces so you're not
blocked: on your repo's GitHub page, click **Code > Codespaces > Create codespace
on main**. Everything is preinstalled there. Then post your problem (see below)
so we can fix your laptop setup later. If Codespaces itself is the problem, post
right away.

## Getting help {#getting-help}

### Post on Discussions

Include all four of these, so someone can help on the first reply:

1. Where you're working: Codespaces, or your own Windows or Mac computer.
2. The setup step you were on.
3. The **exact** error text, copied as text (not a screenshot).
4. The full output of `uv run python check_setup.py`, if you can run it.

Answering a classmate's setup question counts toward participation.

### Ask an AI assistant (with the right context first)

Generic AI advice often conflicts with this course's setup. It may tell you to
`pip install numpy`, install Anaconda, or create a new environment, and those
make things worse here. Paste this context **first**, then your problem.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (sign in with your WSU account) is free and works well
for this.

```
I'm setting up a Python course environment. The setup is fixed and I must not
change it:
- Editor: GitHub Codespaces (VS Code in the browser), or Positron on my own
  computer (built on VS Code).
- Python environment: managed by uv. My repo has pyproject.toml, uv.lock and
  .python-version (Python 3.13). The environment is built with `uv sync` into a
  .venv folder in the repo.
- Code lives in a private GitHub repo. In Codespaces, Git signs in
  automatically; on my own computer, Git signs in with Git Credential Manager
  (Windows) or the GitHub CLI (Mac).
- The repo checker is `uv run python check_setup.py`; [!!] lines are problems.

Rules for your answer:
- Do NOT suggest pip install, conda/Anaconda, a new virtual environment,
  changing pyproject.toml or uv.lock, or a different Python version.
- Fixes should use: uv sync, choosing the .venv interpreter or kernel in
  Positron, moving the repo out of a cloud-synced folder, or Git/GitHub
  settings.
- Give me ONE step at a time, tell me what I should see if it worked, and wait
  for my result before the next step.

Where I'm working: [Codespaces, or my own Windows/Mac computer]
What I was doing: [setup step or command]
Exact error text: [paste]
check_setup.py output: [paste, if available]
```

Two more prompts that help:

- **Before running a Git command you're unsure about:** *"Before I run
  `[command]`, explain in plain language what it will do, and whether it can lose
  any of my work. Don't suggest alternatives unless it's risky."*
- **When an error message makes no sense:** *"Explain this error in plain
  language for a beginner: what it means, the most likely cause, and the first
  thing to check. Error: [paste]"*

If an AI assistant helped with your setup, say so in PS01's AI usage note, the same as for any
problem set.
